reason: The elite figures in this passage—specifically the Israelite leaders (Joshua and the princes/נְשִׂיאִים)—are portrayed unfavorably. They are depicted as being deceived by Gibeonite cunning (עָרְמָה), failing to consult God's guidance (אֶת־ פִּי יְהוָה לֹא שָׁאָלוּ), and making a rash covenant without proper discernment. Furthermore, the community's complaint against these leaders (וַיִּלֹּנוּ כַל־הָעֵדָה עַל־הַנְּשִׂיאִים) explicitly highlights their unfavorable status. Additionally, the foreign kings mentioned at the outset are shown gathering in apparent hostility. The passage demonstrates the elite's lack of wisdom and their vulnerability to deception.
